corpus.content: Nova uses a retrieval augmented generation pipeline that parses documents, creates overlapping chunks, retrieves evidence, builds a grounded prompt, and streams the answer.
User passwords are protected with salted PBKDF2 HMAC SHA256 using 310000 iterations and constant time comparison.
Short lived access tokens expire after ten minutes and remain only in browser memory. Rotating refresh tokens are stored in HttpOnly Secure SameSite cookies and hashed server side.
Server Sent Events deliver language model tokens incrementally from FastAPI to the React client and allow generation cancellation and initial connection retry.
Hybrid retrieval combines BM25 lexical ranking with FAISS dense vectors. Reciprocal rank fusion merges the two ranked lists.
Backblaze B2 stores uploaded document and vector index artifacts. Conversations should not remain in object storage: relational users, refresh sessions, and conversations belong in PostgreSQL.
The responsive interface supports light dark and system themes, keyboard shortcuts, reduced motion, voice input, animated transitions, error recovery, and accessibility checks.
The readiness endpoint contacts the configured AI provider and verifies that the selected Groq or Ollama model is available before startup completes.
The FastAPI backend deploys to Render while the Vite React frontend deploys to Vercel. Vercel proxies same origin API paths to Render and Docker Compose supports local development.

Secure upload validation checks extension, MIME allowlist, magic byte signature, PDF page complexity, size limits, and optional ClamAV malware scanning. Stored upload filenames are generated as UUIDs, while DOCX archive expansion limits prevent zip bombs.

The external PDF downloader blocks localhost private link local reserved and multicast IP addresses. HTTP redirects are not followed automatically: it resolves DNS, validates each redirect and connected peer address, reducing DNS rebinding risk.
SQLAlchemy stores users refresh sessions and conversations in PostgreSQL. Alembic manages schema migrations and row locking prevents lost conversation updates across replicas.

Document parsing embeddings and reindexing run as background jobs. The API returns a job identifier, and the frontend tracks indexing progress by polling it while Redis RQ shares work across replicas.

The quality benchmark reports retrieval metrics including Recall at K, mean reciprocal rank, citation precision, citation recall, faithfulness, unanswerable accuracy, and latency. It measures questions with no answer and compares three retrieval modes in an ablation: BM25, dense FAISS, and hybrid RRF.
